top.description: Julianna Funk/Alamy Break open the bubbly, light the candles and get ready to party – New Scientist is 70 years old! Times have certainly changed since we published our first issue in 1956. Back then, some scientists had proposed that our carbon dioxide emissions were warming the planet, but the idea was controversial. Biologists were only beginning to unpick how DNA, whose structure had just been elucidated by Francis Crick, James Watson, Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, encoded the instructions for building organisms. The founders of this magazine couldn’t have envisaged the many ways that the web and smartphones would change daily life. We are even old enough that what once seemed futuristic is now pleasantly quaint. Launching our first website, Planet Science , in 1995, we declared that, “As the technologies mature, quite soon and at a terminal near you, it may be possible to hear interviews with well-known scientists”. Our digital offering has expanded greatly since then, with these sorts of interviews now available across our podcast and video channels. That said, we also speculated that it might be possible to “manipulate three-dimensional models of molecules” on a future version of our website, which we still haven’t quite managed to deliver. To mark our anniversary, we have put together a timeline of the biggest breakthroughs of the past 70 years . I enjoyed diving into our archives in search of how we reported era-defining moments. Our assessments haven’t always been on the money: after Yuri Gagarin’s space flight in 1961, for example, our correspondent declared “it is almost physically impossible for [the US] to beat the Russians to the moon”. Are these the most spectacular and intriguing beetles in the world?
top.description: The glorious flower chafer Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum What animal is older than the dinosaurs and accounts for nearly a quarter of species on Earth? It is the magnificent beetle, an insect whose wings rest underneath a hard, protective case that often displays beautiful colours and intricate ornaments. “Wherever you stand on the land surface of the Earth save only for Antarctica, you are never more than a few metres from a beetle,” writes Maxwell Barclay in Interesting Beetles , which showcases some of their stunning variety. The main image shows the glorious flower chafer ( Howdenypa gloriosa ), a stunning opalescent green and blue. Its sleek flight from flower to flower, which takes place with the wing cases closed, unlike the clumsier flights of beetles with open wing cases, has attracted attention from aerospace engineers. They have fitted some flower chafers with tiny wireless transmitters to better understand how they manoeuvre while flying. Below is the Colorado potato beetle ( Leptinotarsa decemlineata ), which has a destructive relationship with humans. After the potato was introduced to North America, this striped beetle started to prefer spuds to native foods and quickly became a worldwide pest. Advertisement The Colorado potato beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Below, the carbuncle frog-legged beetle ( Sagra carbunculus ) shows off the buff hind legs that earned it its amphibian-inspired name and serve it well in battle – or when competing for an iridescent mate. The carbuncle frog-legged beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum The specimens in these images are taken from the archives of the Natural History Museum in London, where Barclay is senior curator in charge of beetles. It was difficult, he writes in his book, to choose which to include, “because each of the 400,000 beetle species has an interesting story to tell”. The violin beetle ( Mormolyce phyllodes ) shown below makes up for being an inelegant flyer by having a unique body shape that allows it to blend in with fallen leaves and winged seeds of trees in the steamy tropical rainforests where it resides. The violin beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Finally, the desert fog-basking beetle ( Onymacris bicolor ) shown below is another master of adaptation that can survive in places as arid and harsh as the Namib desert in southern Africa. The desert fog-basking beetle Lucie Goodayle/Trustees of the Natural History Museum Barclay writes that beetles can not only survive in all these habitats, from potato fields to tropical forests and deserts, but that they are an integral part of each of them. top.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
top.description: null United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28 , and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.) ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update. Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit. In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance. Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure. Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

top.title: Convoy attack: WoPU hails Tinubu over clemency to 78 suspects
top.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young Working People United (WoPU) has commended President Bola Tinubu for granting clemency to the 78 individuals arrested in connection with the attack on his presidential convoy in Abuja, describing the decision as an act of statesmanship, magnanimity and compassionate leadership. In a statement by its National Coordinator-General, Prince Williams Akporeha, the group said the President’s decision demonstrated his commitment to national unity, reconciliation and peace despite the gravity of the incident. WoPU said the gesture reflected Tinubu’s willingness to prioritise forgiveness and national harmony over confrontation. According to the statement, “President Bola Ahmed Tinubu has once again demonstrated the depth of his compassion, fatherly disposition, and unwavering commitment to the welfare of all Nigerians. “By extending clemency to the 78 suspects arrested over the attack on his convoy, the President has shown that leadership is not merely about the exercise of authority but also about mercy, understanding, and the pursuit of national harmony.” The group described the decision as a demonstration of the President’s belief in second chances and peaceful coexistence, adding that it would help prevent the incident from deepening divisions in the country. WoPU said the gesture was consistent with the objectives of the Renewed Hope Agenda, which seeks to build an inclusive, prosperous and stable Nigeria. It urged Nigerian youths to emulate the President’s example by embracing dialogue, patience and responsible civic engagement. The movement also cautioned young people against allowing themselves to be used by individuals or groups seeking to promote violence and instability for political interests. “It is imperative for Nigerian youths to remain vigilant and responsible. They must resist every attempt by unscrupulous elements to use them as instruments of violence, lawlessness, and political disruption. “The future of our nation lies in peaceful participation, constructive engagement, and unwavering faith in democratic institutions,” the statement added. The group also urged youths to appreciate the administration’s policies and reforms, which it said were designed to promote long-term economic growth, social stability and national development. It reaffirmed its support for the Tinubu administration’s reforms and developmental initiatives, expressing confidence that the Renewed Hope Agenda would deliver positive outcomes for workers, entrepreneurs, artisans, professionals and other Nigerians. WoPU, a civic and socio-political movement comprising workers, traders, artisans, professionals, entrepreneurs and grassroots stakeholders across the country, said it would continue to mobilise support for the President’s vision of a prosperous and united Nigeria beyond 2027. Agbese, a Labour Party member representing a constituency in Benue State, said engagement between the legislature and the national oil company was necessary to ensure that the objectives of the PIA translated into measurable improvements in the petroleum industry. He urged other government agencies to adopt similar open-door approaches in their dealings with the legislature, stressing that transparency and institutional collaboration were essential to effective governance. The conference, themed, “Petroleum Industry Act Implementation: The PIA, Corporate Governance and Legislative Oversight,” was organised in collaboration with the Office of the Speaker of the House, Rep. Abbas Tajudeen. He stressed that NNPCL’s commercial autonomy must be matched with corporate accountability, noting that the freedom to make business decisions must come with responsibility for their consequences. nigeria.title: Viral Video: ‘We recovered 12 AK-47 rifles, kidnap victims’ – Military defends engagement with bandits
nigeria.description: By Kingsley Omonobi The military has defended its engagement with armed bandits in Kwara State, dismissing allegations of fraternisation with terrorists. They added that the interaction led to the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The Joint Task Force, Operation Savannah Shield, said the engagement, captured in a video circulating on social media, was part of a security initiative to recover illegal weapons and secure the freedom of abducted persons. In a statement, the task force said the interaction involving military personnel, Department of State Services (DSS) operatives and the armed bandits should not be misconstrued as a compromise of the Armed Forces’ responsibilities. The statement, signed by the Acting Deputy Director, Army Public Relations, 9 Division/Operation Savannah Shield, Lieutenant Colonel Ibrahim Shittu, said the armed elements had indicated their willingness to surrender their weapons and release their captives. Shittu said the development followed sustained military operations that had put the bandits under intense pressure, leaving them with the options of surrendering or being neutralised. He said the engagement resulted in the recovery of 12 AK-47 rifles and the release of 10 kidnapped persons. The task force described the outcome as evidence of the effectiveness of its non-kinetic approach, which complements ongoing military offensives against terrorism and banditry. It explained that its operational strategy combined military action, intelligence-driven engagements and other non-kinetic measures to address security challenges. The task force added that individuals willing to surrender would undergo appropriate security screening and other applicable legal procedures. Shittu also said surrendered combatants must not be harmed at the point of surrender, in line with the Law of Armed Conflict, international best practices and established rules of engagement. He stressed that accepting the surrender of armed elements was a recognised and legitimate military outcome, not an indication of unprofessional conduct or compromise. The task force reaffirmed the Armed Forces’ commitment to defending Nigeria’s territorial integrity and protecting lives and property. It urged members of the public to disregard what it described as misleading interpretations of the video and avoid spreading unverified information capable of undermining ongoing security operations. Operation Savannah Shield assured Nigerians that it would continue to provide updates on its activities through its official communication channels. nigeria.title: Explosion heard in Riyadh, Saudi capital; missiles intercepted
nigeria.description: A powerful explosion rattled homes in Riyadh on Wednesday, AFP journalists and residents said, as Yemen’s Iran-backed Houthis pressed their campaign of attacks against the kingdom. The Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis also said they intercepted two cruise missiles — the latest in weeks of strikes targeting military, civilian and oil infrastructure. Later on Wednesday, the coalition said it had intercepted two drones launched by the Houthis in the Riyadh and southern regions, after Saudi authorities had issued and later lifted an alert for the southern Sharurah governorate. Residents said Wednesday’s explosion came without warning, with no mobile-phone alert issued beforehand as is usually the case during aerial threats. “The explosion was extremely loud,” said a resident in northern Riyadh. “Hearing a blast without receiving a warning is very frightening.” An AFP journalist said doors throughout her home swung open and the lights briefly went out. The location of the explosion was not immediately clear, but residents told AFP they saw smoke near Riyadh’s airport in the northeast of the city. In October, a deadly attack targeting Riyadh’s King Khalid International Airport killed 14 people and injured hundreds, forcing the suspension of flights for two weeks. Within minutes, the Saudi-led coalition fighting the Houthis said its air defences had intercepted and destroyed a cruise missile launched by the group towards the Riyadh region. Earlier, the coalition had reported intercepting another cruise missile also heading for the same region. Saudi civil defence authorities also said they had activated early warning systems in the southern regions of Jazan, Najran and Khamis Mushait, near the Yemeni border. The Saudi-led coalition, which backs neighbouring Yemen’s internationally recognised government in its war with the Houthis, has battled a surge in attacks since hostilities reignited in July. The long-running civil war in Yemen, one of the world’s poorest countries, had been largely dormant after a ceasefire went into effect in 2022. The Houthis are now nearing Aden, the government’s interim capital, having made sweeping territorial gains since the war resumed. Since the summer, more than 1,600 people have been killed and over 300,000 displaced by the fighting, according to the United Nations. nigeria.title: Senate passes bills establishing research fund, granting medical college PhD powers
nigeria.description: By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has passed two bills seeking to provide a framework for research funding and expand postgraduate medical education in Nigeria. The bills are the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill, 2026, and the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, 2026. Both bills were passed on Wednesday after consideration of their provisions, clause by clause, at the Committee of the Whole and subsequent third reading. Their passage followed the presentation and consideration of reports by the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund, chaired by Senator Mohammed Dandutse (APC, Katsina South). Presenting the reports, Dandutse said the National Research and Innovation Development Fund Establishment Bill sought to establish a sustainable funding mechanism for research, development and innovation across the country. He said the proposed legislation also provided for the establishment of the National Council on Research and Innovation, which would provide strategic direction, policy oversight and supervision for Nigeria’s research agenda. According to him, the proposed fund would support research institutions and provide a dedicated funding framework for addressing the country’s development challenges. He added that the fund and the council would work together to strengthen Nigeria’s research, scientific, technological and innovation capabilities. On the National Postgraduate Medical College Act Amendment Bill, Dandutse said the proposed amendment sought to expand the academic and institutional functions of the college. He explained that the amendment would empower the college to establish academic programmes and award Doctor of Philosophy (PhD) degrees in specialised medical disciplines. The areas include clinical medicine, dentistry, basic medical sciences, pharmacology and other related fields. Dandutse further explained that the amendment would empower the college’s Senate to develop, administer and supervise the proposed doctoral programmes. He said the programmes would be subject to accreditation and regulation by the National Universities Commission (NUC) to ensure compliance with prescribed academic standards. According to him, the proposed changes are intended to provide a framework for advanced medical education, clinical research and specialised medical training in the country. business.description: Bitcoin Magazine Coinbase Says Its AI Blocked $4.7 Million in Deepfake Elon Musk Scam Coinbase (COIN) said its AI scam-prevention agent stopped about $4.7 million in customer funds from reaching scammers who used a deepfake of Elon Musk to pitch a fake Tesla crypto giveaway, blocking roughly 91% of the money customers tried to send. The exchange described the incident in a Tuesday blog post, part of a weekly series on consumer protection. It said the system worked “with no humans in the loop.” Those two figures imply customers tried to send about $5.2 million, and that roughly $460,000 still left their accounts. Coinbase did not say how much reached the scammers. A livestream that wasn’t real The scam ran during Tesla’s “flying car” demo. Scammers set up a YouTube livestream that looked like the real broadcast, with a deepfake Musk, on-screen wallet addresses and a QR code. The stream promised to double any crypto sent to it, and more than half a million people watched, Coinbase said. Over about two hours, hundreds of Coinbase customers tried to send millions of dollars to the addresses on screen. Many were long-time users. Coinbase did not say when the fake stream ran or which coins customers tried to send. The company stressed that its platform was not breached. “Nobody was hacked,” Coinbase wrote. “No Coinbase account was broken into, no password stolen, no credential phished.” That is what makes giveaway fraud hard to stop, since most defenses look for activity the account holder did not authorize, and here the customers logged in and pressed confirm themselves. “Our systems can see risk signals in real time. They can’t see intent,” the post said. How the agent works Coinbase said its defense has three parts. Machine learning models first score outgoing sends in real time, watching for giveaway patterns, brand impersonation and newly created wallet addresses. The goal, the company wrote, is “to catch the danger, not the customer.” When a send is flagged, a scam-specific agent takes over, looking up context, naming the scam pattern, explaining how giveaway schemes work and asking questions meant to make the story fall apart. Each reply is scored for confidence before the customer sees it, so the system knows when a situation needs more friction. The agent had never been trained on this kind of con, Coinbase said. Deepfake giveaways tied to a live product launch were not in its training data. “It recognized the shape of the scheme anyway,” the company wrote, pointing to the promise to multiply funds, the deadline of a live event and a transfer that could not be reversed. business.title: South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says
business.description: Bitcoin Magazine South Korea Set to Let 3,500 Companies Buy Bitcoin, Report Says South Korea’s Financial Services Commission plans to publish guidelines next week that would let about 3,500 listed companies and professional-investor firms buy bitcoin and other crypto for investment, a local news agency reported Wednesday. The guidelines will be released alongside the government’s draft of the Digital Asset Basic Act, the country’s planned framework for the crypto industry, according to the report . The FSC plans to convene its Virtual Asset Committee to coincide with the release. The FSC itself has not publicly announced a date for either release. If it lands next week, the move would come one year and nine months after the regulator laid out its roadmap for corporate crypto access in February 2025. A roadmap that stalled That plan opened the market in stages, with nonprofits and crypto service providers coming first, and only to sell. Since June 2025, Korean nonprofits have been able to cash out crypto they receive as donations, and World Vision made the first such trade, selling donated ether on Upbit. Exchanges have also been allowed to sell their own holdings to cover operating costs. Coinone and DigitalX, formerly Korbit, have done so several times after filing disclosures. The second stage, which lets listed companies and firms registered as professional investors trade crypto for investment, was slated for the second half of 2025. It never arrived. The holdup is market plumbing. Corporate orders are large, and even Korea’s biggest exchanges have limited room to absorb them without moving prices. “If companies come into the market and trade 5 billion won each, even an exchange like Upbit would struggle to take that volume,” an unnamed industry official told News1. Large trades would normally run through over-the-counter desks, and Korea does not yet have rules governing how those desks operate. What the Basic Act adds The Digital Asset Basic Act is meant to close that gap. It would split crypto service providers into separate business types and set entry and conduct rules for OTC desks, brokers and other operators, the report said. The government’s draft is expected to go to the National Assembly next week. Lawmakers want it passed quickly. The Assembly’s Political Affairs Committee aims to process the bill by January, timed to the implementation of the U.S. GENIUS Act, the stablecoin law. Rep. Min Byung-duk of the Democratic Party said at a recent forum that he intends to “wrap it up by Jan. 9.” The 5% question The report did not describe what the corporate guidelines will contain. entertainment.description: Beyoncé becomes the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram If you have ever wondered what triple digits look like on music’s biggest stage, Beyoncé just gave everyone the answer. The Houston-born global music superstar has officially become the first artist in history to reach 100 career Grammy nominations, hitting the milestone with her latest nod for “ Morning Dew ( Donk )”, which is nominated for Best R&B Solo Performance at the 69th Annual Grammy Awards (2027 Grammys). Released in July 2026 ahead of the 20th anniversary of her sophomore album B’Day, “Morning Dew (Donk)” puts her in a category alongside Kehlani , Victoria Monét , Jill Scott , and Nigerian star Tems . To put the 100-nomination milestone into perspective, no other recording artist has ever crossed into triple digits since the Grammys began. Beyoncé had previously been tied with her husband, Jay-Z , at 88 nominations each before breaking that tie in 2024 with 11 nods for Cowboy Carter to reach 99—and this latest recognition pushes her even further ahead as the artist with the highest number of Grammy nominations in history. Beyoncé holding her three Grammy trophies at the 67th Annual Grammy Awards in 2025. Photo Credit: Beyoncé/Instagram It is also a good reminder of how long she has been doing this at the highest level. Beyoncé’s Grammy journey started all the way back in 2000 as part of Destiny’s Child with “Bills, Bills, Bills”, and across more than two decades as a solo artist, group member, and collaborator, she has built a record that keeps stretching further ahead of the pack. Alongside holding the title for the most Grammy nominations of all time, she is already the most awarded artist in Grammy history with 35 wins, a record she first broke in 2023 when she surpassed late conductor Georg Solti ’s 31 trophies. She pushed that tally even higher at the 2025 Grammys, taking home three awards—Album of the Year and Best Country Album for Cowboy Carter, as well as Best Country Duo/Group Performance for “II Most Wanted” alongside Miley Cyrus . entertainment.description: Report identifies next SME digitization opportunity: connecting payments with day-to-day business management. 94% of SMEs surveyed find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, yet only 29% currently use one, pointing to untapped demand for tools that connect payments with business management. Integrated payment and business solutions can give financial institutions a more holistic view of SME cash flow and support more tailored financing solutions over time. Small- and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) in Nigeria have largely moved beyond the first stage of digital payment adoption, but a productivity gap remains. According to Visa’s new survey for its Pay and Get Paid 2026 report, most of the SMEs surveyed in Nigeria use digital payments, showing how firmly digital commerce has taken root in the country’s small business economy. However, many SMEs still manage the related financial and operational tasks separately, with only 29% currently using an integrated solution that connects payments with broader business management. The report shows that financial admin and disconnected tools create friction for SMEs, with surveyed businesses citing challenges in tracking outstanding invoices (14%), keeping payroll records organized (19%), and preparing financial reports (16%). These pain points reflect a disconnect between payments and the operational tasks that follow, with some businesses juggling multiple systems to keep their business running. The appetite for a more connected approach is clear. According to the report, 94% of SMEs find an all-in-one payment and business solution appealing, reflecting strong interest in tools that can bring payments and key business operations into one experience. However, adoption has yet to catch up: only 29% of SMEs currently use an integrated payment and business platform. The report points to several perception barriers that may be slowing adoption. Businesses cited that they already have manual processes that work (8%), that an integrated platform may disrupt their current way of working (8%), or that they do not trust relying on a single provider (7%). These findings suggest that broader adoption will depend on helping SMEs better understand how integrated tools can be relevant, accessible, and scalable for businesses at different stages of growth. At the same time, the experience of SMEs already using integrated solutions suggests a strong value case. The report found that Nigerian businesses using an integrated tool or platform report 93% satisfaction, with 88% reporting efficiency gains, including reductions in the time and effort required to manage their business. Beyond efficiency, integrated platforms may also create new opportunities for financial institutions to deepen SME relationships by using richer payments and business-management data to better understand cash flow patterns, support risk assessment, and potentially enable more relevant lending solutions over time. In June 2023, ahead of the 66th Grammy Awards, the Recording Academy announced the creation of the Best African Music Performance category. Its creation was a recognition of how far African music had travelled globally, and Nigerian artists were at the centre of that movement. From Burna Boy ‘s Ye , CKay ‘s Love Nwantiti , Wizkid ‘s explosive Essence , to Rema ‘s globally successful Calm Down and others, Nigerian artists became drivers of African music’s global expansion. Afrobeats – the umbrella term often used internationally to describe much of contemporary African popular music, although many Nigerian artists have rejected it for its tendency to limit the range of music coming out of the country – became an established genre globally. While Nigerian and African music have always travelled beyond their respective countries, the era of streaming and digital platforms has accelerated how quickly global audiences discover and engage with the music. African music became increasingly established in the West and other parts of the world, creating greater recognition for its artists and sounds. The Grammys’ decision to introduce a category specifically recognising African music performances was an important step in that direction, beyond the recognition African artists had previously received in categories such as Best Global Music Album. Although the creation of the Best African Music Performance category was celebrated throughout the continent, there seems to be a monopoly, or something close to it, of Nigerian music in the category. technology.title: California tells Waymo to take the next exit after freeway mishaps
technology.description: Waymo has suspended driverless freeway rides across the US after California regulators intervened over robotaxis entering construction zones and trying to bypass highway patrol vehicles. California's DMV banned Waymo from offering driverless trips on its freeways on Wednesday, November 11. The same day, Waymo pulled the handbrake on its freeway services countrywide. The move affects all areas in which Waymo operates on freeways, including San Francisco, Los Angeles, Miami, Phoenix, and Austin. The Alphabet-owned company has not indicated how long the suspension will last. Waymo says freeway testing will continue with trained specialists behind the wheel. Jonathan Groveman, spokesperson for the California DMV, told the Associated Press that the organization imposed the ban following two incidents involving Waymo's robotaxis that posed an "imminent hazard to public safety." On November 5, three of the company's driverless cars entered an active construction zone on US 101 near Burlingame, south of San Francisco. The second incident occurred the following day, and in footage shared widely online , a Waymo vehicle can be seen trying to drive around highway patrol vehicles conducting a traffic break – a maneuver used to slow or stop traffic. "The Department determined that Waymo's driverless freeway operations pose an imminent hazard to public safety due to recurring incursions by its vehicles into active construction zones where construction workers, vehicles and equipment are present," Groveman said in the statement. Groveman said the DMV had already imposed restrictions and required corrective action following similar incidents on May 18. Waymo subsequently recalled nearly 4,000 cars after some were caught ignoring road closure signs and cones designating construction zones in Phoenix and San Francisco. A separate recall covered software affecting nearly 3,800 robotaxis over problems including slowing on high-speed roadways and driving into floodwater . A Waymo spokesperson said that despite California's temporary ban, its robotaxis continue to operate on city streets across the US. "Safety is at the foundation of everything we do," they said. "Following recent freeway construction zone encounters on US 101 in California that did not involve any injuries or collisions, the California DMV has implemented an operating restriction on freeway operations in the state. "In alignment with our safety-first principles, we have also temporarily restricted freeway operations across our other operating markets to evaluate our performance. Our ride-hailing service continues to operate safely on surface streets, serving over half a million trips each week. "We are working with the California DMV and other state officials diligently and responsibly to resume freeway operations." Other nuisances and hazards caused by errant Waymos include clogging traffic in thick fog , driving into telephone poles , and killing cats and dogs . ®

technology.title: Microsoft's official Python agent framework hijacked to distribute malware
technology.description: Microsoft’s official agent framework package hosted on PyPI has been hijacked and now installs info-stealing malware, multiple security research firms have discovered. CEO Satya Nadella may be on stage trying to wow investors and customers at his company’s annual Ignite conference , but somewhere in the bowels of a building in Redmond his open source team is likely panicking at what appears to be unauthorized access to an administrator account on Microsoft’s Github organization. The problem package is Microsoft’s agent-framework, versions 1.26.1 and 1.26.2, researchers reported late yesterday and this morning . According to OX Security, version 1.26.1 was reverted to a safe version, but the attacker later uploaded 1.26.2 through Microsoft’s official PyPI publisher account, suggesting that, at least at the time of their report, the credentials hadn’t been locked down. Safe to say, but if you find either version in your environment assume you have some account security work to do. Microsoft agent-framework for Python boasts nearly 200,000 downloads a month and is used to build and deploy AI agents. As of those latest releases, it’s also being used to exfiltrate environment variables, credential files, and other secrets for Azure, Git, Docker, Hugging Face, and other sensitive developer services. To make matters worse, the package never needs to be imported to do its dirty work – all it takes is a Python interpreter with the package installed to start up – the infected package still pulls the genuine 1.26.0 version of Microsoft’s agent-framework in order to keep itself running and looking legitimate, while in the background it gathers up credentials, encrypts them as a base64-encoded chunk of JSON, and sends them off to a webhook.site address hard coded into the malware. It appears from researcher accounts that this is made to act fast, as the malware isn’t persistent and only runs as long as the malicious version of the agent-framework remains in a site-packages directory. What it does do, however, is not just look for credentials in the environment: It actually starts calling for new ones and collecting them, too. In particular, the malware requests fresh identity tokens from GitHub Actions, Azure DevOps, and Azure itself, which are exfiltrated to the same webhook site. “That combination of passive theft and active token requests makes it especially dangerous in cloud build environments, because even short-lived tokens are useful when they're exfiltrated right away,” said researchers at OpenSourceMalware. The agent-framework GitHub repo is offline as of writing. It’s been pointed out online that Microsoft’s repo for ONNX Runtime , an AI accelerator, is also offline. technology.title: MongoDB snaps up Firebolt to bring transactions and analytics under one roof
technology.description: MongoDB has acquired analytical database specialist Firebolt in another attempt to bring transactional and analytical workloads onto one platform. The document database vendor carved out its patch of the database market with flexible, JSON-like documents rather than rigid, predefined table structures. Developers put it to work in web, mobile, ecommerce, and content management applications. It has since branched out to offer a data platform it says is ready for the age of AI and AI agents working across transactional environments, promising scale, speed and reliability. Firebolt was founded in Israel in 2019. It built a cloud-native data warehouse based on the notion of automatically and transparently merging and compacting files as they are ingested. Speaking to The Register in 2020 , then CTO Eldad Farkash claimed this slashes the amount of data users need to load into the system, accelerating query performance and improving concurrency. Firebolt raised $100 million in Series C funding in 2022 at a reported valuation of $1.4 billion. MongoDB has not disclosed the acquisition price. But what will it get, and what does that mean for MongoDB users? In a blog post , the company said: "By integrating Firebolt into MongoDB's Intelligent Data Platform, we're bringing a high-performance analytics engine to where your operational data already lives. technology.title: Cyber insurers now want proof you can actually recover
technology.description: Cyber insurance pricing has cooled. Marsh’s Global Insurance Market Index shows global cyber rates falling for a 13th consecutive quarter, with US rates recently stabilizing after the ransomware-driven spikes of 2020 and 2021 . Part of the reason rates are lowering is because carriers are imposing stricter requirements that determine if you will qualify at all. A major global carrier recently stopped writing law firms altogether because of claims volume, and brokers expect healthcare and managed service providers (MSPs) to be next. The newest requirement is the one many MSPs are least ready for: proof that you can actually recover. This is what insurers really want to see, and meeting the bar is harder than it sounds. Why insurers stopped taking backups on faith In a recent webinar with cyber insurance provider Beltex , the familiar list of requirements came up first: Multifactor authentication (MFA) on external access and privileged accounts Endpoint detection and response (EDR) on every endpoint A staffed 24/7 team where managed detection and response (MDR) is required, and timely patching. Backup is now joining that list, and for good reason. For years it was assumed that having backups and a green job status was good enough. Claims have shown otherwise. Now, attackers go after backup infrastructure to make their ransomware more effective, and an untested restore can re-infect the production network. Beltex described an MSP that restored a client directly from backup without involving the insurer. The attackers were still in the environment, and the ransom reportedly doubled. So, carriers are asking for proof. Some want evidence of a successful restore within the last six months, and some insurance applications must be signed by a C-level executive rather than the IT director to put ownership behind it. Proof of speed matters as much as proof of recovery Being able to recover is only half the question, because time is where claim costs balloon. Insurers, it turns out, don’t object to paying claims. They object to paying big ones. Beltex’s favorite example involved an 85-person firm hit through a zero-day firewall flaw. Their MDR solution contained the intrusion in about 20 minutes, forensics confirmed two servers were touched, and clean backups had the firm fully functional within 36 hours. The claim came in at around $85,000. Compare that with downtime and business interruption: a firm billing $10,000 a day that is offline for a week loses $70,000 in income before recovery costs and claim submission. Yet large servers can take four to 24 hours to restore. That is why underwriters care how fast you can come back and how successfully. Where you recover is the other half Speed raises a second problem: where do you restore to? technology.title: PowerShell 7 heading into Windows as 5.1 hits the end of the road
technology.description: Microsoft has confirmed that, at long last, PowerShell 7 will come bundled with Windows, while the venerable PowerShell 5.1 begins its long retirement. It has been a long time coming, although PowerShell 5.1 isn't going away immediately. It will, however, " be removed from a future version of Windows ," and Windows Server 2025 and Windows 11 26H2 are the last versions to include PowerShell 5.1 enabled by default. After that, PowerShell 5.1 will be available as a Feature On Demand (FOD) before eventually shuffling off into the sunset, while PowerShell 7 takes over automation duties. PowerShell 5.1 is now more than ten years old and runs on the .NET Framework. PowerShell 7 is its cross-platform, open source successor, but compatibility isn't seamless. PowerShell was the brainchild of Jeffrey Snover , who sought to bring script automation to Windows at a time when graphical user interfaces were king. He recalled executives telling him "admins don't want command line interfaces," and "exactly what part of effing Windows is confusing you?" but eventually won the argument, and we reckon countless Windows administrators owe him a debt of gratitude. PowerShell 5.1 hasn't had many new features for years. "PowerShell 7 is the modern PowerShell: the one we develop in the open, across platforms, and where new features go," wrote Jason Helmick, a senior product manager on Microsoft's PowerShell team. But compatibility niggles remain. The two can run side by side, so existing scripts won't have to move immediately. Finding and testing everything scattered across an enterprise estate, however, could keep administrators occupied for some time. Microsoft also has unfinished work on the bundled version's MSIX packaging, including support for running as SYSTEM, DISM cmdlets, and machine-wide settings. Those gaps matter for scheduled tasks, services, and management scripts. Despite the deprecation, PowerShell 5.1 will continue to receive updates based on the lifecycle of the Windows version on which it runs. It will eventually be removed based on usage data and "communicated in advance," according to Microsoft. Administrators have time to prepare, but checking which scripts run unchanged, which need work, and which still depend on 5.1 won't happen by itself. "Including PowerShell 7 in Windows is a milestone we've been working toward since PowerShell went cross-platform," Helmick wrote, although the bundled release is still ahead. Microsoft says PowerShell 7 will arrive with the next Windows release, but hasn't named it. 27H2, anyone? ®

Times have certainly changed since we published our first issue in 1956. Biologists were only beginning to unpick how DNA, whose structure had just been elucidated by Francis Crick, James Watson, Rosalind Franklin and Maurice Wilkins, encoded the instructions for building organisms. The founders of this magazine couldn’t have envisaged the many ways that the web and smartphones would change daily life. We are even old enough that what once seemed futuristic is now pleasantly quaint. Launching our first website, Planet Science , in 1995, we declared that, “As the technologies mature, quite soon and at a terminal near you, it may be possible to hear interviews with well-known scientists”. Our digital offering has expanded greatly since then, with these sorts of interviews now available across our podcast and video channels. That said, we also speculated that it might be possible to “manipulate three-dimensional models of molecules” on a future version of our website, which we still haven’t quite managed to deliver. science.title: ULA traces Vulcan Centaur rocket failure to 'inadequate fuel supply' to 1st-stage engines
science.description: null United Launch Alliance (ULA) is getting a handle on why its Vulcan Centaur rocket failed over the weekend. That failure, which occurred during a launch from Florida's Space Coast on Sunday (Nov. 15), led to the loss of 40 Amazon Leo internet satellites . ULA soon traced the anomaly to Vulcan Centaur's first stage , and it has now pinpointed the problem area even further. "While work remains to determine cause, preliminary indications are that the low booster thrust was the result of inadequate fuel supply from the vehicle to the BE-4 engines, not from the performance of the engines," ULA wrote in an update today (Nov. 18). This is good news for Blue Origin , Jeff Bezos' aerospace company, which builds the BE-4. Two of these engines power Vulcan's first-stage booster, and they're also key to Blue Origin's New Glenn rocket: That heavy lifter features seven or nine BE-4s in its first stage, depending on the configuration. (New Glenn has its own issues at the moment; it exploded during a test on May 28 , and Blue Origin is working to return the powerful rocket to flight.) ULA had already said that Vulcan's six solid rocket boosters (SRBs) and its Centaur V upper stage — which employs a different engine, the RL-10 — seem to perform well on Sunday. Further analysis is firming up that conclusion, according to today's update. Vulcan has had issues with its SRBs in the past. On the rocket's second and fourth flights — which launched in October 2024 and February of this year, respectively — an SRB nozzle burned through and fell off about 30 seconds into flight. On both occasions, Vulcan overcame the problem and successfully delivered its payload to orbit. In the wake of the February flight, ULA and Northrop Grumman, which builds the SRBs, tweaked the nozzle design — a fix that apparently worked, based on Sunday's nominal performance. Vulcan Centaur rises into the sky on Nov. 15, 2026. (Image credit: ULA) Sunday's launch was the fifth ever for the two-stage Vulcan Centaur, the successor to ULA's workhorse Atlas V rocket. Vulcan debuted in January 2024 and has now experienced issues on three of its five flights, though Sunday's was the only one that ended in failure. Vulcan was out of action for about nine months after the February SRB issue. It's unclear how long its current grounding will last; that depends on what ULA's anomaly investigation, which the U.S. Federal Aviation Administration is overseeing, ends up finding.

science.title: What Is the Moon Base?
science.description: 7 Min Read What Is the Moon Base? This article is for students. NASA is returning astronauts to the Moon – and this time they will spend more time on the lunar surface. The Moon Base is humanity’s first lunar outpost . It will be a place where astronauts live, work, and explore. Artist’s concept depicting astronauts, habitats, rovers, power systems, and cargo operations supporting sustained human activities at the Moon Base near the lunar South Pole. NASA ______________________________________________________________________ Words to Know outpost: a station or base located in a remote, distant place infrastructure: the basic framework and systems that make up a larger building or organization terrain: the physical features, shape, and layout of the surface of a piece of land, including its slope and elevation regolith : the layer of loose, fragmented rock and mineral dust covering most of the lunar surface ______________________________________________________________________ Where Will the Moon Base Be Built? The Moon Base will be built in the lunar South Pole region. This area was selected for its unique lighting conditions and potential for scientific discovery. Near the lunar South Pole, the Sun stays low on the horizon. Some areas can receive extended periods of sunlight. Other areas stay in shadows for long periods of time. In some craters, sunlight may never reach the surface at all. Areas that receive extended sunlight could be good for generating solar power. Longer sunlight hours are also good for navigating and exploring. Areas that remain in shadows are some of the coldest areas on the Moon. In these locations, scientists hope to find deposits of frozen water ice. When Will the Moon Base Be Constructed? The Moon Base will be constructed in three phases. Each phase will build on what is learned along the way. Phase One is taking place right now. Over the next few years, NASA and its partners will send robotic missions to explore the lunar South Pole region. They will test new technologies and practice landing on the Moon. This phase will include multiple different landers and lunar terrain vehicles. These missions will conduct science experiments and look for the best locations for building the Moon Base. Phase Two is planned for 2029-2032. During this period, NASA will begin setting up long-term infrastructure . This includes things like power systems, cargo transportation, and communications hardware. These components will be set up across multiple locations. science.title: 'A shotgun marriage': Why are NASA's SkyFall Mars helicopters riding on a nuclear rocket?
science.description: null The pace is picking up on building, testing, and plotting out the flight paths for a trio of NASA Ingenuity-class helicopters to investigate Mars after riding there on a nuclear-powered rocket. NASA's Skyfall mission will see those mini-choppers dropped off at Mars by the space agency's Space Reactor-1 Freedom (SR-1) rocket, the first fission nuclear-powered interplanetary spacecraft slated for launch in late 2028. After its cruise phase and initial Mars flyby in 2029, that nuclear carrier craft will make a second Mars approach in the Fall of 2030 to unleash a SkyFall entry capsule outfitted with a fleet of small aerial vehicles that will soar across the Red Planet . But some experts are questioning why NASA is combining two such high-profile missions into one. "It is clear that SkyFall was approved for programmatic or political reasons," said Scott Hubbard, former director of NASA's Ames Research Center and the first Mars Program Director (aka the " Mars Czar ") at NASA Headquarters, told Space.com. "The connection to Space Reactor-1 seems to me to be a bit of a shotgun marriage, a tech-demo piggybacking on another mission as an opening bid for a 'nuclear NASA.'" Shotgun marriage? Hubbard is a retired adjunct professor of aeronautics and astronautics at Stanford University. He is a major voice in shaping Red Planet exploration goals, drawing upon his expertise as NASA's former foremost Mars authority. His understanding is that the basic concept had been developed as a follow on to Ingenuity, an attempt to move beyond a technology demo and into a science platform. Hubbard said that combining these two observations, the outcome presents "an unusual set of management issues." Since the SkyFall mission concept first appeared, he said, the usual sequence for a science mission is reversed. "The science community is having to scramble to back into a set of requirements and objectives that match the SkyFall capabilities. Fortunately the community is very creative," said Hubbard, "and the basic Planetary Decadal objectives are very broad." Decadal surveys reflect a broad consensus within the scientific community and provide detailed insights into the strategic priorities and mission directives set for the next decade across key scientific domains, including planetary exploration. science.title: Homo erectus survived on mainland Asia 215,000 years longer than we thought
science.description: Reconstruction of a specimen of Homo erectus S. ENTRESSANGLE/E. DAYNES/SCIENCE PHOTO LIBRARY Preserved teeth from two caves in southern China indicate Homo erectus lived on mainland Asia as recently as 184,000 years ago. That is recent enough for the species to have met later groups like the Denisovans. It seems these Chinese H. erectus were living in a tropical rainforest – an environment where the species has not previously been found. “We’ve got this late surviving population, and we’ve got this rich story of how they were living,” says geochronologist Kira Westaway at Macquarie University in Sydney. Advertisement H. erectus was one of the first species in our genus, Homo . It was also the first species of hominin we know for sure migrated beyond Africa. The earliest H. erectus fossils are from Africa 2 million years ago, but by 1.8 million years ago they were living in what is now Georgia on the border between Europe and Asia. Eventually the species spread further east into what is now China. They even made it to the island of Java. Read more The 85-million-year timeline of human evolution The most recent fossils identified as H. erectus are from Java and are between 117,000 and 108,000 years old . However, it’s been thought the species vanished much earlier from mainland Asia. Until the discoveries from China announced today, the most recent securely dated H. erectus were from around 400,000 years ago. Around this time, other hominin groups emerged, like the Denisovans who lived in East Asia. “The assumption would have been that erectus is basically no longer there, because they have evolved into a Denisovan population,” says molecular palaeontologist Frido Welker at the University of Copenhagen in Denmark. Welker, Westaway and their colleagues investigated two caves in southern China. Baxian and Naxian are both limestone caves, about 15 kilometres apart. They were initially excavated by Chinese teams led by Yingqi Zhang at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology in Beijing and Wei Wang at Shandong University. science.title: Quantum trick lets you share your location super securely
science.description: NIST’s campus in Boulder, Colorado NIST Financial institutions and critical infrastructure could be made far more secure in the near-future using quantum particles. For years, researchers have predicted that quantum particles could enable someone to share their location, and to verify someone else’s, in a way that is exceedingly difficult to hack. This would allow one branch of a bank to confirm that a request for funds or client information is coming from another branch and not from a hacker. Likewise, hackers could be stopped from trying to remotely control a power grid, a nuclear plant – or even commercial freezers, which have recently been hacked across Europe . Gautam Kavuri at the University of Colorado Boulder and his colleagues have now shown that quantum devices really can provide such location verification, offering a level of security impenetrable to most hackers. Advertisement Read more Inside the company selling quantum entanglement “From a security perspective, it’s sort of the gold-plated Rolls Royce of protocols. It’s got the best security you can have in principle, while making the least assumptions,” says team member Krister Shalm at the National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST) in Colorado. “And you can actually do it.” In the researchers’ experiment, two verifier devices had to confirm the location of a third device called the prover. Each device was in a different location: the verifiers were 195 metres apart in different labs and the prover was in a third location between them. Kavuri says it was important for these devices to be in different rooms on the NIST campus, rather than all in the same lab, because this is closer to a practical scenario in the real world. The devices were connected with electrical cables and optical fibres and could exchange quantum particles of light that had been connected into pairs through the inextricable link of quantum entanglement . To begin the new quantum position verification (QPV) protocol, a verifier would send one photon from an entangled pair to the prover and, simultaneously, each verifier would also send a random number that instructed the prover on which particle property to measure. Next, the prover sent the outcome of that measurement to both verifiers. They used the time it took to receive this information to calculate the prover’s position. First, quantum information, such as that carried by particles of light, can never be copied or cloned surreptitiously . Additionally, the researchers leveraged a procedure called a Bell test , which is specific to entangled particles, and would be failed if a hacker tampered with them. The net effect was that any conventional strategy for faking the position would set off one of these quantum safeguards. (Image credit: Dark Energy Survey/DOE/FNAL/DECam/CTIO/NOIRLab/NSF/AURA. http://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/. Acknowledgment: PIs: G. Narayan & T. Murphey (University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign) Image processing: M. Zamani & D. de Martin (NSF NOIRLab)) A new supernova has been spotted exploding in the spiral galaxy NGC 1433, about 50 million light-years from Earth. What is it? Researchers have discovered a new supernova called SN 2026ahvu. A Type Ia supernova, this event took place in a system with two stars orbiting one another (also known as a binary system), in which typically one star is an exploding white dwarf . During most type Ia supernovae, the white dwarf pulls material away from the other star until enough accumulates on its surface to create an explosion. Finding galaxies where stellar explosions are taking place isn't a rarity. However, this supernova is unique in how early it was captured. If the supernova were starting to dim, researchers might infer that the event was ending. However, according to details shared when it was first spotted, as well as later observations, this supernova was discovered while getting brighter. This indicates that the supernova was likely caught early in the process of exploding, providing researchers with a unique opportunity to observe the event as it is taking place. By exploring observations of the galaxy before, during and (in the future) after the supernova event, researchers can investigate this type Ia supernova and how it affected the system in which it took place. Why is it incredible? Scientists made this discovery using ATLAS, or the Asteroid Terrestrial-impact System, which is a robotic astronomical survey made up of telescopes across both hemispheres. ATLAS is designed to spot incoming near-Earth objects like asteroids before they can reach Earth. It's essentially an asteroid impact early warning system. But just because that's what the system is designed for doesn't mean that's all it can do. The system can also spot other objects moving through space and, in this instance, it was able to capture observations of this supernova. Following its initial discovery, other observations of the supernova were made using NOIRLab's Dark Energy Camera (DECam) and Gemini South telescope.
